title: Who Made a Greek Book in Venice?
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Mediterranean Travels
description: Attribute ten contributions to Greek printing in Venice around 1500 to the people who made them, and watch the network of editors, printers, financiers, teachers, and patrons grow.

educational.topic: Who Made a Greek Book in Venice?
learningObjectives: Attribute ten contributions to Greek and humanist printing in Venice around 1500 to the people who made them, attributing at least 8 of 10 correctly on the first attempt.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Attribution quiz on a growing network (one confirmed link at a time)
keyQuestions: Which jobs did it take to make a printed Greek book?
Which of those jobs did Aldus himself do?
Where do the Cretans appear in the network?
commonMisconceptions: Aldus did all the work himself, so every contribution belongs to him.
The editor and the printer were the same person.
Venice's Greek printing was Italian work, with no Greek or Cretan makers.
A rival press was an enemy of learning rather than another route to it.
assessmentOpportunities: First-choice score on ten cards (mastery: 8 of 10).
How many of the ten were born on Crete (3).
